newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS - BASF to sell tape unit to KOHAP.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - BASF to sell tape unit to KOHAP.

text.p: German chemical firm BASF AG, in a surprise move, on Tuesday said that South Korean textile group Kohap Ltd would take over its worldwide magnetic tape unit instead of Turkey's RAKS Holding AS.
BASF said in a statement that Kohap would take control of its Magnetics arm from January 1 for an undisclosed amount. The statement made no mention of a previous letter of understanding with RAKS.

Although a deal with RAKS seemed sealed after it was announced in August, BASF's supervisory board in September demanded that other potential buyers be considered for one of the world's best known tape brands.

The chemical giant's supervisory board had expressed concern that the Turkish group was too small and questioned its ability to run Magnetics, which posted sales of 1.5 billion marks ($991.4 million) last year and employs 3,700 workers.

Analysts said the deal with Kohap was seen as preferable to one with RAKS. BASF shares were sharply higher after the news, ending electronic trade up 1.24 marks, or 2.5 percent, at 50.50 marks, ahead of the market trend.
"Although I don't think the proceeds from the sale will be that great, I think they'll get more than from the Turkish group," said Ronald Koehler, chemicals analyst at BHF Bank.
BASF has long been trying to sell the loss-making Magnetics group to concentrate on its core chemical, drug and agricultural business.

Analysts have said it should get rid of Magnetics at any price. It has absorbed 600 million marks in subsidies from BASF in the last five years and is expected to post a 1996 operating loss of around 20 million marks.
BHF Bank's Koehler said he did not expect many jobs to be lost after the handover of Magnetics to Kohap.
"The group could undertake some restructuring, but Kohap is not very strong in this area and there won't be much over-lapping business. BASF has already made big cuts at Magnetics," he said.
"Kohap is not a big player in this market and they will want to build up their position in Europe," Koehler said.
Kohap is South Korea's leading integrated producer of synthetic fabrics and yarns, with 1995 turnover of 913 billion won ($1.12 billion).
The firm made net profits of 4.8 billion won in 1996, but in the first half of 1996 profits fell sharply.
BASF said more information about the sale would be released at a news conference on Wednesday.
BHF Bank's Koehler said the sale would have a relatively neutral effect on the results of the entire BASF group.
